text.title: Graceful Offboard Script Failure Modes
text.summary: 6 antipatterns observed when offboarding a bad-fit client. Each pairs a symptom, a root cause, and a concrete fix keyed to a rule in 01-core-rules.xml.

antipattern.symptom: The script says "we have not been able to give you the service you deserve"; the client repeats it as "they admitted they could not cope" to two prospects in the agency's pipeline.
antipattern.root-cause: Guilt or conflict avoidance wrote the framing; nobody checked the draft against the banned list.
antipattern.fix: Rewrite every sentence about the engagement as a fit and alignment statement; run the banned-phrase check; keep every sentence about the client neutral or positive.

antipattern.symptom: The agency announces a two-week wind-down on a contract with 60 days' notice; the client invoices for the shortfall and the exit becomes a dispute.
antipattern.root-cause: The termination clause was not read before the date was chosen.
antipattern.fix: Quote the clause id, set the last service date at or beyond what it allows, and state how prepaid or committed periods are delivered or refunded.

antipattern.symptom: The client asks three times for their ad account and domain credentials after the last service date; the story circulates that the agency held their assets.
antipattern.root-cause: No asset inventory was built; transfers happened on request rather than on schedule, and an open invoice was used as leverage without a clause.
antipattern.fix: Build the per-asset inventory with owner, method and date; transfer client-owned assets on schedule regardless of dispute unless a quoted clause allows otherwise.

antipattern.symptom: The script recommends a partner agency; the client contacts them and is declined; the client now distrusts both.
antipattern.root-cause: The alternative was named from memory, not confirmed.
antipattern.fix: Confirm willingness with the alternative before naming them; record the date and channel; offer the warm introduction in the script.

antipattern.symptom: The offboard arrives as an email on a Friday afternoon; the client's first reaction is to their board, not to the agency.
antipattern.root-cause: The account owner avoided the conversation and let the written script carry the message alone.
antipattern.fix: Deliver live first by the named account owner; send the written script and handover plan within one business day, containing nothing that was not said on the call.

antipattern.symptom: No contact after the handover; six months later the ex-client is asked about the agency and remembers only the exit.
antipattern.root-cause: No T+30 feedback request was scheduled; the offboard was treated as the end of the relationship rather than a change in it.
antipattern.fix: Schedule the T+30 NPS or feedback request; ask promoters for a testimonial or referral; thank detractors and ask one question; never argue.
